FINDING_ID: R3_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.86  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` can silently drop failure accounting for active models that never respond, because it iterates only over `responses.items()` and never compares against the expected active/allocated model set.** This is related to prior “missing responses” concerns, but the deeper missed issue is cross-area corruption: a non-responding active model receives neither failure detection nor `role_assignment.record_failure(False/True)`, so its failure-history denominator stops advancing while other models accumulate history. That biases `phi_hist` in `RoleAssignment.reassign()`, making flaky silent models look artificially better than models that did respond and were assessed. It also leaves `_perf_history` and transport-failure history untouched, so repeated omission can evade exclusion/escalation entirely. PROPOSED_FIX: derive the expected responder set from the round allocation or active model set, synthesize a failure record for each missing model (at minimum `EMPTY`/`TIMEOUT`-like policy based on protocol), and record a per-round success/failure bit for every active model, not just responders.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.83  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **Round processing trusts caller-supplied `responses` keys over `ModelResponse.model_id`, and the two can disagree without detection.** The code loops `for model_id, response in responses.items():` but passes `response` into `detect_failure()` and later calls `get_recovery(model_id, ...)`. If a caller supplies `responses = {"m1": ModelResponse(model_id="m2", ...)}`, events and underperformance history are attributed to `m2` inside `detect_failure()`, while recovery history and role-assignment failure history are recorded under `m1`. That splits one physical incident across two logical identities and corrupts failure history, activity state, and monitoring. This is distinct from the broader integrity-check findings because it is a specific internal identity-split bug at the dict-entry boundary. PROPOSED_FIX: validate `key == response.model_id` for every response before processing, and reject or normalize inconsistent inputs.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.81  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`findings` are accepted without validating that each finding’s `model_id` belongs to a responding and currently active model, allowing capability updates and convergence state to be poisoned by unauthenticated findings.** Earlier reports noted lack of general integrity checks, but the missed cross-cutting consequence is that one forged or stale `Finding.model_id` feeds three subsystems at once: convergence clustering, diminishing-returns yield, and `update_fingerprints()` attribution. A caller can make an idle/excluded model appear productive by injecting findings under its ID, or make another model appear highly duplicative/low-quality. PROPOSED_FIX: validate that every finding’s `model_id` is in the current active set and is associated with an actual accepted response from that round before admitting it into any downstream metric.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.79  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`FailureHandler` can permanently poison a model’s underperformance state via duplicate evaluation of the same response, because `detect_failure()` mutates `_perf_history` on every call with no idempotence guard.** Prior work noted history mutation generally, but the missed edge case is replay sensitivity across orchestration retries, monitoring hooks, or caller mistakes: re-processing the same `ModelResponse` appends the same performance sample again, shortening the effective persistence window and potentially triggering `UNDERPERFORM` earlier than intended. Since the method has no round/model deduplication key, accidental double invocation changes system state. PROPOSED_FIX: track `(model_id, round_idx)` evaluations and make performance-history updates idempotent per response identity, or separate pure classification from state mutation.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.84  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **Failure recovery side effects are incomplete for `ABORT`: the PM is not removed from `active_models`, so `FailureHandler.should_abort()` and `active_models` can report a logically live PM after an unrecoverable PM failure.** `get_recovery()` returns `ABORT` for repeated PM transport/protocol failures, but only `EXCLUDE` mutates `_active_models`. The manager happens to terminate on `critical_failure`, but the failure handler’s own state remains inconsistent: `active_models` still contains a PM that the policy has declared fatal. Any external consumer inspecting failure state before or after termination sees a contradictory picture. PROPOSED_FIX: on `ABORT`, either mark the failed PM inactive immediately or maintain an explicit terminal-failure flag that `active_models`/`should_abort()` honor consistently.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.76  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`check_dispatch_feasibility()` evaluates a single model in isolation and therefore can approve individual dispatches that are jointly infeasible once multiple tasks are assigned to the same model.** The method takes `(model, task_load)` and checks only that one aggregate load against uncertain `L`, but the public API and surrounding comments suggest a pre-dispatch safety mechanism for the allocation path. Used naively per task, two tasks can each pass the check against an empty load baseline yet exceed capacity together. This is a missed cross-cutting design flaw between the feasibility extension and orchestration surface. PROPOSED_FIX: make feasibility checks allocation-aware by accepting current committed load plus incremental task load, or expose a batch/round feasibility API instead of a per-call scalar helper.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.72  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **Core dataclasses accept NaN and infinite numeric values, and several downstream comparisons turn those into silent false negatives instead of hard failures.** This was only broadly alluded to before; the missed concrete impact spans multiple areas: `response.response_time = nan` bypasses timeout detection because `nan > threshold` is False; `severity = nan` can propagate into `max()`/means and contaminate convergence; `token_demand = nan` or `L = nan` can poison load calculations and feasibility predicates; `criticality = nan` breaks sort and redundancy semantics. The system does not reject non-finite numbers at construction or processing boundaries. PROPOSED_FIX: validate finiteness and expected ranges for all externally supplied numeric fields in config, `Task`, `Finding`, `ModelResponse`, and `ModelSpec`.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.77  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **Round progression and event semantics are internally inverted: `process_round()` emits `ROUND_COMPLETE` before any failure analysis, convergence check, stop check, FSM transition, or fingerprint update has happened.** Prior reports mentioned misleading events, but the deeper issue is that downstream consumers observing the stream can act on a “round complete” signal while the manager is still mutating core state and may yet terminate on failure. The same event type is also reused later for “Fingerprints updated,” conflating lifecycle completion with a post-processing side effect. PROPOSED_FIX: emit `ROUND_START`/`ROUND_PROCESSING`/`ROUND_COMPLETE` at distinct lifecycle points, reserve `ROUND_COMPLETE` for the final committed state, and use a separate event type for fingerprint updates.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.74  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ConvergenceDetector.add_round_findings()` allows the caller to overwrite an existing round index in place, which can retroactively rewrite historical evidence without any monotonicity or append-only guarantee.** This is distinct from the already-found duplicate round-index bug: even with unique FSM indices, any external caller can call `add_round_findings(1, ...)` twice and silently replace round 1 findings, durations, and adoption delta. Cumulative caches are invalidated and recomputed, so the detector’s history is mutable after the fact. That breaks auditability and makes repeated processing non-reproducible. PROPOSED_FIX: reject duplicate `round_idx` inserts unless an explicit overwrite mode is requested, and surface historical mutation as an error in normal operation.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.69  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`FailureHandler.detect_failure()` can classify a response from an unknown model as non-failing and seed internal history for that unknown ID, because unknown model IDs fall through several lookups with permissive defaults.** `_timeout_threshold()` uses a default tau, `_expected_performance()` returns 0 leading `_performance_metric()` to return 1.0, and `_perf_history.setdefault()` creates history for the unknown model. If the content is non-empty, parseable, and format-compliant, the unknown response is accepted as fine. This opens a state-spoofing path and undermines model-pool integrity. PROPOSED_FIX: reject any response whose `model_id` is not in the configured model set and active set before failure classification.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION: 0.71  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`RoleAssignment.record_failure()` only appends booleans for models explicitly touched by the caller, so per-round failure history lengths diverge across models and the “mean failure rate” penalty becomes incomparable.** This is not just a bookkeeping nuisance: a model evaluated in every round has denominator = total rounds, while an omitted model has denominator = only rounds where it was processed. The penalty therefore measures “failure rate conditional on being recorded,” not failure rate over system rounds. In conjunction with silent missing-response handling, this materially biases COL reassignment. PROPOSED_FIX: update failure history for every active model once per round with an explicit success/failure/missing outcome, or track histories keyed by round index rather than append-only booleans.  

FINDING_ID: R3_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.73  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The event interface claims PM can trigger dynamic `RETRY/REALLOCATE/EXCLUDE`, but no event path carries a decision channel back into manager state, so the monitoring interface is observational only despite its control-language contract.** Existing findings noted missing emitted recovery events; the missed deeper issue is architectural: `ManagerEventStream` is one-way and `DynamicManager` exposes no handler for PM commands, overrides, or acknowledgements. The docstring overstates the interface’s role in real-time control. PROPOSED_FIX: either downgrade the monitoring interface documentation to read-only telemetry, or add an explicit command API/state machine for externally requested recovery actions.  

These are new findings beyond the listed prior rounds.
